title: JANUS I0 two-workflow retro SHA-256 trial, t0 vs t0+120 seconds: completed result

implementation.t0_action: Python secrets.token_bytes(32) -> SHA-256 prediction, save JSON artifact and GitHub step summary before launching SEND
implementation.t1_action: Wait to t0+120s; generate independent OS random 32-byte payload and SHA-256 BEFORE reading receive artifact
implementation.t2_action: Download receive artifact; verify timestamps, trial ID and bytewise SHA equality; publish result

comparison.interpretation: Under the independent-random SHA-256 baseline, no full match occurred. This neither establishes nor comprehensively falsifies physical retrocausal communication.

evidence_provenance: Run logs and GitHub Actions artifacts checked on 2026-11-05. Artifact SHA-256 digest values are GitHub-reported ZIP digests, distinct from the trial SHA-256 values.
evidence_retention: GitHub Actions artifacts set to 30 days; append-only result JSON retains values and digests.
next_step: A controlled, physically meaningful test requires an independently specified source of pre-target predictions and an externally auditable target-generation protocol. The I0 SHA engine alone is not a retrocausal receiver.
epistemic_limits: CI success means execution succeeded, not that the hypothesized physical channel exists.
Two independent random SHA-256 values normally differ; no exact match was observed.
A future exact match would require independent source verification and replication before any retrocausal inference.
This one-shot run used no actual mechanism for transferring data into the past.
